top_concerns: Probability distribution under‑weights CKD‑related anemia and metabolic acidosis.
Over‑estimation of non‑diabetic glomerular disease without supporting serology or biopsy.
Questionable inclusion of alcohol‑related liver disease and hemolytic anemia lacking objective data.
Need for additional labs (CBC, iron studies, liver panel, ABG, renal imaging) to resolve uncertainties.
review_summary: The junior differential captures the major organ‑system issues and links most high‑severity labs to plausible diagnoses. Adjustments are needed: increase weight for diabetic nephropathy, CKD‑related anemia, and metabolic acidosis; decrease weight for speculative entities (alcoholic liver disease, hemolysis, renovascular disease). Additional targeted investigations are required to confirm or refute the lower‑probability diagnoses.
